clue.text: Child with blanket nursing cold beginning to take cough medicine

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the child's name wraps around what follows
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: Linus is the Peanuts boy who always carries his security blanket
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
the first letter of take

explanation.surface: A child clutching a blanket and suffering a cold is starting on some cough mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: C and T together sit inside LINUS; 'beginning to' takes just the first letter of 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a thick syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough.

clue.text: The French paper that is socialist

blocks.note: le is French for the
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A French newspaper described as socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftie is an informal term for someone holding left-wing political views.

clue.text: Feed Canton, having grub to go around

blocks.note: nosh is British slang for food

explanation.surface: Feeding the Chinese city of Canton, with takeaway food to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Canton looks like the old name for Guangzhou; here it is a Swiss canton.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish someone is to feed them, providing what they need to grow.

clue.text: Alluring woman exhausted, wasting year cutting hair

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so the year's letter is dropped
something cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: an exhausted supply is empty
Y is the abbreviation for year
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A seductive woman, worn out after a year of hairdressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' reads as tired, but here it means used up, as an emptied supply is.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is a woman who deliberately entices or seduces others.

clue.text: Key player — oops! — hints carelessly about a vote

indicators.note: something done carelessly ends up jumbled, so these letters are reordered
about means surrounding, so the reworked letters go around the rest

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written
a voter marks a cross, X, on the ballot

explanation.surface: A pianist fumbles, dropping clumsy hints about how to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' suggests an important person or a pianist; a saxophone has keys too.
explanation.definitionFit: A saxophone is worked by pressing keys, so a saxophonist is a player of a keyed instrument.

clue.text: Ride around we hear to purchase tool for harvest

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spoken phrase stands for a word spelt differently

blocks.note: to purchase is to buy, and a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops

explanation.surface: A farmer is told to go out and buy a harvesting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to bicycle is to travel about on a bike, so it means to ride around.

clue.text: Party turned up to support British person

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party arriving to back a British individual.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that supports another sits below it, so B goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is British slang for a person, as in 'an odd bod'.

clue.text: Island initially celebrating All Fools' Day

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: the first letter
April Fools' Day is the first of April, APR plus I for one

explanation.surface: An island holding an April Fools' Day party.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples off southern Italy.

clue.text: Deer caught a bone round top of upland

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a rib is a bone
O is a round shape
the first letter

clue.text: Enter the complex network

clue.text: Bewildered G-man punched by knucklehead

clue.text: Settle in upper chamber

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

clue.text: One returning to identify Charlie

the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a fool, so it is a synonym for a stupid person.

clue.text: Open then shut local room

to bar a door is to shut it

explanation.surface: Instructions for a room that is opened and then closed again.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British pub; its public bar is the plainer of its rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The public bar is one of the rooms in a pub, the 'local' a Briton drinks at.

clue.text: Expert account about a large old Western figure

taken as written

O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.walkthrough: A buff is a keen enthusiast, as in a film buff; 'about' puts the three short letters between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo Bill Cody was a famous frontiersman and Wild West showman.

clue.text: Funny elf, fourteen, who could be fair game

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of the three words are used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' sounds like a legitimate target; read it as a game at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel of fortune is a spinning prize wheel found as a game at funfairs.

clue.text: The cigar's turned to a pile of ash long ago

indicators.note: something turned is changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all nine letters

explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the cigar ash: the German parliament building burned in the 1933 fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag building in Berlin was gutted by fire in 1933, leaving it a ruin.

clue.text: Severe redundancy leaving area strapped for cash

clue.text: Northern Irish leaders formula: ultimately a peaceful state

the van, short for vanguard, is at the front
the last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' belongs to the definition: the final letter of 'formula' supplies the A.

clue.text: Drink finished off by players mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: slang for killed

clue.text: Butt of agenda uncovered

blocks.note: the letters inside the two words, with the outer ones dropped

clue.text: Somewhat slowly, Clark uncovered poor sector of the city

the first, third and fifth letters
